brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: 6 cells in a compact cluster holding half-depth bins (about 48 mm deep), a size suited to screws and other small hardware. Outer faces are capped and the joints bolted together.

6 separate bin parts: bin:0,0,0 (2 compartments), bin:-1,1,0 (2 compartments), bin:1,0,0 (3 compartments), bin:0,1,0 (3 compartments), bin:-1,0,0 (open) and bin:1,-1,0 (open). That is 14 sections in total.

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organiser from six full hex base cells joined in a compact cluster at level 0, each holding its own half-depth bin. Two bins are open, two have 2 compartments and two have 3, which gives 14 sections in all. I capped every open outer face with solid end caps (18 caps) and bolted the joints between cells (9 joint bolts), for 30 parts in total. The print estimate is about 2.7 kg of filament and about 64 hours. For display only, I put heaps of M3 screws in 10 of the compartments; some compartments were too small for the screw props, so they stay empty. The check passed with no rule errors, the mesh collision check reads clear and there are no prop warnings.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
